<reflection>
The product-added experiment did not dramatically distinguish product-involvement mechanisms (M12, M17) - they perform similarly to others. This suggests product may not be strongly deactivating. M19, M2, M13, M18 remain leading - all involve bimolecular catalyst behavior. M4, M5 continue to fail. M20 is now clearly weaker than the leaders. Still need to differentiate among M19, M2, M13, M18, M9.

Key insight: 
- M2: reversible dimerization (2cat <=> cat2)
- M13: irreversible 2cat→inactive_cat2 
- M19: cat + catS → inactive_cat2S (requires substrate bound)
- M18: 2catS → inactive_cat2S2 (requires 2 substrate-bound species)
- M9: cat → inactive (first order decay)

Discriminating: at low substrate, little catS forms, so M18, M19 would show slower deactivation while M13 and M9 would still deactivate. At high cat + low S, M13 (2cat→) should dominate; M19/M18 which need catS, should be weaker.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
To distinguish among the leading bimolecular-catalyst mechanisms, I'll run at HIGH catalyst but LOW substrate. This creates conditions where:
- [catS] is small (substrate-limited)
- [cat] is large

Predictions:
- M13 (2cat→inactive): Rapid deactivation since it depends on [cat]² - high loss even before much turnover
- M2 (2cat⇌cat2 reversible): Reversible sequestration, depends on [cat]²
- M19 (cat+catS→inactive): Moderate - needs catS formation
- M18 (2catS→inactive): Slow - needs high catS
- M9 (cat→inactive): Independent of [cat]² scaling — different pattern
- M11 (S+cat→inactive): Depends on [S], so slow at low [S]
- M14 (catS→inactive): slow since catS is low

So very different predictions among these. Also low S allows observation of whether reaction completes (if catalyst survives, turnover completes; if not, reaction stalls).

S=0.3, cat=0.1, P=0. This tests catalyst-squared vs catalyst-first-order effects at substrate-limited conditions.
</hypothesis>
